report.summary: Two review-recommended findings: the new Redis session cache introduces an unmodeled external data store for Restricted session tokens, and the newly added github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 dependency has no third_party_dependency assertion.

findings.title: Session tokens now persisted in an external Redis store not represented in the model

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "session tokens" classification=Restricted — Bearer tokens proving a signed-in session

evidence.note: New Cache type holds a Redis client: "Cache stores session tokens in Redis so instances share log-ins."
Raw session token used as the Redis key ("session:"+token) and stored with the user id, so the Restricted asset leaves the process boundary
NewCache connects to an arbitrary addr with no TLS or auth options set on redis.Options

relevance.justification: A Restricted information asset is now written to a new external store that no threat, control, or DFD element in the model describes.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the 'login service' threat model: this PR added internal/session/cache.go, which stores the Restricted 'session tokens' information asset in an external Redis instance (redis.NewClient at internal/session/cache.go:16, SET of key "session:"+token at internal/session/cache.go:22, no TLS or auth configured). Add modelling for this new surface: either a data_flow_diagram with a data_store for the Redis session cache, a process for the session package, and a flow carrying 'session tokens' across the trust boundary, or at minimum a new threat block (STRIDE Spoofing/Information Disclosure) describing theft of session tokens from the shared Redis cache, with controls covering transport encryption, Redis authentication, and whether raw tokens (versus hashes) are used as keys.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a threat (and DFD data_store/flow) in app.tm.hcl covering session tokens stored in the external Redis cache.

findings.title: New go-redis dependency has no third_party_dependency assertion

model_excerpt.quote: third_party_dependency "identity provider" uptime_dependency=degraded — Hosted IdP handling SSO log-ins

evidence.note: github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 v9.7.0 added as a direct requirement
Package imports github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 and the service now depends on a reachable Redis instance for session lookups

relevance.justification: The model lists only the IdP as a third-party dependency, while session resolution now depends on an external Redis service added in this PR.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: this PR added github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 v9.7.0 (go.mod:6) and internal/session/cache.go now resolves session tokens from an external Redis instance (internal/session/cache.go:24-26), so the login service cannot authenticate sessions if Redis is unavailable. Add a third_party_dependency block named "session cache (Redis)" to the 'login service' threat model with a description of what it stores (Restricted session tokens) and set uptime_dependency to the correct value ('hard' if log-ins fail without it, 'degraded' otherwise).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third_party_dependency "session cache (Redis)" block to app.tm.hcl with the appropriate uptime_dependency.
